\[
R = \text{the pixels } p \text{ connected to } s \text{ through pixels with } |Y(p) - Y(s)| \le T,
\qquad T = 20
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(s\): The seed pixel
- \(Y\): The brightness
- \(T\): The tolerance

s is the seed pixel and Y the brightness. A pixel joins the region when it matches the seed and a path of matching pixels joins it to the seed. Each step of the path goes to one of the 4 or 8 neighbors. This is how skimage.segmentation.flood grows a region. It is also the region growing with a fixed seed value that Gonzalez and Woods describe. With the color measure, the test is the largest of the three channel differences. The seed is at a percent of the width and height, rounded down to a pixel, so it stays on the same spot when the image is resized.
